html:
The Wirangu are an Aboriginal people of the far west coast of South Australia, around Ceduna and Streaky Bay on the Great Australian Bight.

Their country runs from the sea into the dry country at the edge of the Nullarbor. Neighbours on the map are the Mirning to the west, the Kokatha inland and the Barngarla to the east on Eyre Peninsula. Coastal people fished and gathered shellfish, and travelled inland between soaks and rockholes.

Sheep stations spread along this coast from the 1860s. The Wirangu language almost disappeared, but people have worked to revive it from old records and the memory of elders. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their wider history is in Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Wirangu are an Aboriginal people of the far west coast of South Australia, around Ceduna and Streaky Bay on the Great Australian Bight.
